parts.text:
3
An ion is accelerated in a vacuum by a series of electrodes. A graph of the power supplied to the
ion is plotted against time.
What is represented by the area under the graph between two times?
A
the average force on the ion
B
the change in kinetic energy of the ion
C
the change in momentum of the ion
D
the change in velocity of the ion

hints: Notice the vertical axis is power $P$ in $\text{W}$ and the horizontal axis is time $t$ in $\text{s}$, so the area has units $\text{W s} = \text{J}$.
Recall that power is the rate of transfer of energy, $P = \frac{dE}{dt}$, so multiplying by a time interval reverses the division.
Think what work done on the ion in vacuum becomes if there is no loss - link total energy supplied to kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$.
walkthrough: Identify the graph: $y$-axis is power $P$ supplied to the ion, $x$-axis is time $t$, and we need the area between two times $t_1$ and $t_2$.
State the governing rule: power is rate of energy transfer, $P = \frac{\Delta E}{\Delta t}$, so for varying power $\Delta E = \int P \, dt$.
Interpret the integral graphically: $\int P \, dt$ between $t_1$ and $t_2$ is exactly the area under the $P$ against $t$ graph.
Apply energy conservation in vacuum: with no resistive loss, the energy supplied equals work done on the ion, and work done equals change in kinetic energy, $W = \Delta E_k$.
Therefore the area equals the change in kinetic energy of the ion. This is option B.

A.explanation: Area under a force against time graph gives impulse, not area under a power against time graph.

B.explanation: Power multiplied by time is energy supplied, which becomes the increase in kinetic energy of the ion in vacuum.

C.explanation: Change in momentum is the area under a force against time graph, not a power against time graph.

D.explanation: Change in velocity is related to the area under an acceleration against time graph, not a power against time graph.
